name: ipo-trademark-registration-outcome

task.question: For a UK domestic trade mark application filed 2010-2016 - known at filing: mark text, Nice class coverage, category, mark type, series flag and series size, owner country/region/postcode area, filing date - will the mark reach registration as resolved in the IPO's frozen February-2018 open-data snapshot (Registered date recorded)? Unresolved applications at the snapshot (still in examination, opposition or appeal) are censored, never scored.
task.prediction_time: The application's filing date (Europe/London calendar day; register column 'Filed'). Every shipped feature is a filing-time attribute AS RECORDED IN the one frozen 2018-02-13 snapshot (sha256-pinned): mark text, category, mark type, series flag/count, Nice class booleans and count, owner country/region/postcode area. This is a clearly-labelled RETROSPECTIVE single-snapshot task: no historical operational availability is claimed, and no feature is derived from any other application's record. The outcome observation window is the snapshot itself (filed date .. 2018-02-13), so the target window never precedes the instant.

event_key_note: the gate's clustered event count is distinct positive filing dates - a deliberately conservative same-day reading (marks filed the same day by different owners are in truth independent events; hundreds of distinct dates per split keep the count far above the gate minimum either way). The application-level event key is the trade mark number, unique per scored row
feature_documentation: every shipped feature is a filing-time attribute of the application itself: mark text, category, mark type, series flag/count, the 45 Nice class booleans and their count, owner country/region/postcode area, and the filing date. No shipped column is computed from any other application's record, and no history/aggregate feature exists. Not shipped, with reasons: Status, Published, Registered, Expired, Renewal Due Date (the label source and its post-filing companions); Hyperlink (an Excel formula wrapping the mark number); Name (free-text owner identity, excluded by the frozen handoff design - its removal also removes the trivial same-owner outcome-rate join a solver could otherwise build)
high_cardinality_note: mark_text is near-unique per row and owner_postcode_area carries ~2k outward-code levels; both are declared rather than scored by the single-column AUC check, and the runner's baseline drops string columns over 1000 levels automatically. tm_number is the id column. No high-cardinality column encodes any other row's outcome

known_event.name: in-file snapshot fixtures (UK00000000001 'BASS & Co's PALE ALE'; UK00003171385 'Brexit'; UK00003041794)
known_event.expected_verdict: as recorded in the frozen snapshot
known_event.detail: three named rows asserted against the fetched bytes: the 1876 BASS mark (Registered, Registered date 1876-01-01 - identity/fidelity anchor outside every scored cohort); 'Brexit' UK00003171385 filed 2016-06-25, status Appealed and no Registered date at the snapshot -> censored, excluded from the holdout cohort (exercises the censoring rule); and UK00003041794 filed 2014-02-11, Application Published 2017-12-22 and still unregistered at the snapshot -> censored (the long-examination tail must stay censored, never negative). No external threshold is used by this task; the fixtures pin parsing, dedup and censoring semantics
known_event.source: the fetched snapshot itself (values cross-checked at discovery against the publisher's live register for the Brexit mark)

prediction_instant.citation: register column 'Filed' is the application's filing date - the event time documented in the publisher's own guide (ipo-data-explained-2016, section 5, and the dataset landing page 'IPO trade mark data release', last updated 13 Feb 2018); the question is resolved at the filing event, and the snapshot is an administrative record of applications

row_selection.latest_period_used: 2016-12-31 (scored cohorts are filings 2010-01-01..2016-12-31; the 2017-2018 cohorts exist in the snapshot and are excluded by eligibility, never by outcome)
row_selection.basis: membership is fixed by the filing date alone. The label rule runs after membership: a mark whose outcome is unresolved at the frozen snapshot (still in examination, opposition or appeal) is censored - excluded from scoring and counted per cohort - which is outcome-OBSERVABILITY conditioning recorded as a limitation, never a label-value decision; censored marks are not treated as negatives. Rows with blank or unparseable filing dates cannot be placed on the timeline and are excluded and counted

split_boundaries.holdout: filing years 2015-2016 (window end exclusive; the 2017-2018 cohorts stay an unscored reserve outside the frozen design)

positive_events_note: positives and distinct positive filing dates per split, recomputed from the written rows; the gate re-verifies. Positive rates: train 0.866137, eval 0.839885, holdout 0.862927
id_columns_note: tm_number names one application with one observed outcome in the snapshot; construction keeps one row per distinct mark number (multi-owner duplicate rows keep the first occurrence, 16,909 rows removed and counted; the 22,812 letter-suffixed series sub-marks such as UK0000000052A/B are distinct records and stay). The identifier is unique across the artifact, so no id spans two splits

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one application whose features are its own filing-time attributes as recorded in the single frozen 2018-02-13 snapshot; the intended protocol predicts row-wise from the shipped columns (the shipped benchmark validator passes the whole table to the predictor, so isolated_rows is the design intent of this artifact's row-per-application contract, not a runtime-enforced protocol). Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: the publisher exposes one frozen snapshot and no historical vintages, so no full-row availability ledger can be constructed and no historical as-of availability is claimed - retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup

vintage.evidence: exactly one frozen vintage for every row: the publisher's 2018-02-13 open-data snapshot, fetched as a sha256-pinned 63,238,846-byte zip (3b6063bed36a78e8..., Last-Modified 2018-02-13T13:19:48Z); every shipped value is that snapshot's value of a filing-time attribute. The publisher itself warns the snapshot 'may not be directly comparable' with the live register. No mixing of vintages occurs because no other vintage exists

selection.evidence: membership is fixed by filing date (cohorts 2010-2016); eligibility never reads the label. Censoring excludes 1,002 eligible marks whose outcome is unresolved at the snapshot (21/172/809 per split window, 0.31% of the eligible population) and is outcome-observability conditioning - counted per cohort and recorded as a limitation; the 2017-2018 cohorts are excluded by the frozen eligibility window (16,386 and 5,949 censored there at discovery), not by outcome

limitations: single frozen 2018-02-13 snapshot; no historical vintages exist, so no as-of reconstruction of any feature value and no operational-forecasting claim is possible

owner fields are snapshot-vintage: assignment can move ownership after filing, so owner country/region/postcode may reflect a later owner; a robustness variant dropping owner fields is recorded as a future construction decision
Nice class booleans are snapshot-vintage: classes can be narrowed post-filing, so coverage may overstate what was filed

censoring conditions the scored population on outcomes resolvable within the snapshot: 1,002 eligible marks (0.31%; 631 of them in the 2016 cohort, 1.02%) remain unresolved and are excluded rather than labelled; their exclusion is a recorded selection bias, not a missing check

the label window extends to the snapshot date (up to ~8 years for 2010 filings, ~13-25 months for 2016 filings), so 'registered-by-snapshot' mixes horizons across cohorts; per-year reporting is mandatory when quoting figures

large repeat filers (one owner filing many marks) cluster outcomes statistically; owner Name is not shipped, so a same-owner join is not directly available to a solver, but dependence across one owner's marks remains a caveat for uncertainty estimates
filing-year prevalence drifts (negatives 13.4% train / 16.0% eval / 13.7% holdout): a prevalence shift between splits is a measured property of the cohorts

cross_row_audit.rationale: the plausible cross-row exposure family is reverse-history: a later row at the same entity carrying an earlier row's outcome inside a shipped feature. This artifact cannot carry it: no shipped column is derived from any other row (no history or aggregate features exist), and each trade mark number appears exactly once after construction dedup, so no donor row exists for any scored row. The declared probe executes the same-entity join on the full artifact and measures exactly that: coverage is expected to be zero on every split, and nonzero coverage would mean the dedup failed. Coarser keys (owner country/region/postcode) expose only other applications' own attributes, never the scored row's outcome
cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: the artifact ships public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json, quality.json and summary.json. summary.json carries construction diagnostics only (per-cohort counts, hazard buckets, fixture results, censored-status census) and no per-row labels. No joint label matrix or other solver-visible file exists in the artifact
